verdict: Targa's revenue jumped 35% to $5.6B and profit for shareholders rose 38% to $658M, on record Permian gas and NGL volumes and higher commodity prices.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $2.20 a year ago, on profit attributable to Targa shareholders

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: +18% YoY (non-GAAP profit before interest, tax and depreciation)

kpis.label: Quarterly dividend
kpis.note: Per share, +25% YoY; a rise to $6.00 a year is expected for 2027

segments.name: NGL sales
segments.note: Natural gas liquids — propane, butane and similar fuels separated from raw gas — sold to customers. The biggest revenue line, up on higher prices and volumes.

segments.name: Fees from midstream services
segments.note: Fees for gathering, processing, transporting, fractionating and storing gas and NGLs: gathering & processing $634.2M, NGL transportation & fractionation $111.2M, storage, terminaling & export $128.9M and other $1.4M.

segments.name: Natural gas sales
segments.note: Natural gas sold to customers after processing. Up 36% on higher prices and record Permian inlet volumes.

segments.name: Condensate & crude oil sales
segments.note: Condensate and crude oil separated during gathering and processing and sold to customers.

segments.name: Derivative & other revenue
segments.note: Net gains on commodity derivatives that are not sales to customers ($54.7M of non-hedge gains less $36.6M of hedge losses). A year ago this line was a $50.5M loss, so the swing flatters the comparison.

opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Running the pipelines, plants and terminals day to day — labor, maintenance and taxes on operations.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The cost of pipelines, processing plants and fractionators wearing out over time.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — headquarters, legal and admin.

opex.name: Other operating income
opex.note: A credit: other operating income of $20.8M reduced expenses this quarter.

otherDetail: Other expense of $245.2M, net: $232.8M of interest expense, net, and $22.6M of other expense, partly offset by $10.2M of equity earnings from joint ventures. A further $17.9M of net income belonged to noncontrolling interests — outside partners in some assets — leaving $658.2M attributable to Targa shareholders.
oneTimers: Revenue includes $18.1M of net derivative gains that are not sales to customers — $54.7M of gains on derivatives not designated as hedges, partly offset by $36.6M of hedge losses — which can swing either way with gas prices.
footerNote: Segments use the Form 10-Q revenue split by product and service. By operating segment, Gathering & Processing earned an operating margin of $813.6M and Logistics & Transportation $771.0M in the quarter. Net income in the flow is the $658.2M attributable to Targa shareholders, after $17.9M for noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.title: Commodity sales drove growth
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 35% to $5.6B. Higher NGL, gas and condensate prices added about $802M and higher volumes about $383M versus a year ago, and fee revenue rose 29% to $875.7M.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EBITDA up 18%
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA rose 18% to $1,504M on record Permian inlet volumes and record NGL transportation and fractionation volumes. Targa now expects at least $6.0B of adjusted EBITDA for 2026.

takeaways.title: Dividend set to rise again
takeaways.text: The quarterly dividend is $1.25 a share, up 25% year over year, and management expects to recommend $6.00 a share annualized for 2027 — another 20% rise — while spending about $5.0B on growth projects in 2026.
